label: early original-phase m/k/3/j/h/1 after a b/p/m/q/u prefix
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at steps 2-4 (t=2 holds 53% of mass, t=3 holds 38%). It never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, during the copy phase, or at t>=6. The input token is usually m, k, 3, j, h, 1 (and less often o or 2), usually its first occurrence. Firing is strongest when the earlier tokens come from {b, p, m, q, u}: the top examples are k or m right after a b b prefix, e.g. b b [k] or i b b [k]. The same input token after other prefixes mostly does not fire, so the neuron reads a joint (prefix, current token) state that a simple predicate cannot fully pin down. Precision is low because many early m/k/digit inputs stay below threshold.
